# Underdeep — Handbook and advancements (Stage 8)

## 1. The Underdeep Handbook

**Opening it**: the `underdeep_handbook` item (given once to each player on first arrival in an Underdeep world,
config `handbookOnJoin`; craftable from a book and a stick) or the **H** key (rebindable, works without the item).

**Content** (`assets/underdeep/handbook/pages.json`, generated by `tools/handbook/handbook.py`, which validates
every link, icon and item id):

| Category | Authored pages |
|---|---|
| Getting started | 8 |
| The world (one page per region + travel) | 18 |
| Materials | 4 |
| Wildlife | 4 (+ one generated page per discovered species) |
| Civilizations | 11 (one per civilization after you meet it) |
| People | 5 |
| Economy | 7 |
| Farming | 8 |
| Cooking | 8 |
| Medicine | 4 |
| Homes and camping | 4 |
| Equipment | 15 |
| Controls | 3 |

Total 99 authored pages in 13 categories, plus **generated item pages** for every non-technical item: description,
stats (damage, speed, armour, durability, food, effects, upgrades), **How to get** (real acquisition rules from the
obtainability audit: mined where, dropped by whom, crafted from what, sold by which professions), a **recipe grid**
(crafting/smelting/smithing/stonecutting) and **station recipes**, **Uses** and **Used to make** with links.

**Features**: category list, full-text search (title, aliases, body, item names; ranked), back history,
bookmarks (Mark / Saved, stored client-side in `config/underdeep_handbook_bookmarks.txt`), see-also links,
tutorials covering Stages 1–8 (navigation, wildlife and taming, settlements, talking and companions, trade,
contracts and property, farming, cooking, medicine, hazards, camping, equipment, upgrades, accessories).

**Server authority and discovery**: the server sends each player only the item data and the discovery keys they
are entitled to (`Handbook.Data` / `Discover` payloads). Region pages unlock when the region is visited, civilization
pages when one of its settlements is discovered, species pages when the journal records the species,
discovery-sensitive items only after that player has obtained them. Technical and deferred items are never sent.
The field journal (Stages 3–7) stays the personal record; the Handbook links to it (sneak-use the journal for its
pages) and reads the same discovery state.

## 2. Advancements

147 advancement files in 13 tabs (13 roots + **134 advancements**): start 12, exploration 18, wildlife 13,
civilizations 11, relationships 9, economy 12, agriculture 10, cooking 12, medicine 8, homesteading 8,
equipment 21, adventure 6, mastery 7. Frames: 99 tasks, 30 goals, 18 challenges. A few discovery advancements are
hidden until earned (their contents are private).

**Triggers** (`guide/Advancements`): gameplay code reports real, completed actions with
`Advancements.event(player, event, subject)`, e.g. `harvested`, `cooked`, `tamed`, `settlement_discovered`,
`contract_completed`, `forged`, `upgraded`, `accessory_equipped`, `hazard_met`, `rested` (53 distinct events used by advancements, see
the generator). Each player keeps persistent counters (total and distinct subjects; attachment `underdeep:progress`,
kept on death). The custom criterion `underdeep:event` matches `{event, subject?, min, distinct}` so goals like
"harvest 5 different crops" or "discover settlements of 4 civilizations" are exact. Vanilla criteria
(`inventory_changed`, `consume_item`, `location`, …) are used where they fit.

**Rules**: rewards are experience only, granted once by vanilla's tracker; only challenges announce to chat;
progress is per player (cooperative play: each player earns their own); nothing is ever granted for actions the
player did not perform.

**Migration** (`guide/Migration`, config `advancementMigration`): when a player first joins with Stage 8, journal
species/taming, discovered settlements, companions, property, businesses, learned recipes and met hazards from
earlier versions are converted to counters once, with chat announcements suppressed, so existing worlds do not
spam toasts and do not lose credit. It never invents progress that has no saved evidence.

## 3. Rules for future stages (also in CLAUDE.md)
- Every new player-facing system adds Handbook pages (tutorial + reference) to `tools/handbook/handbook.py` and
  regenerates; item pages come automatically from the audit.
- Every new system reports its completed actions with `Advancements.event` and adds advancements in
  `tools/advancements/generate.py` (keep the total sensible; no grinding counts above what normal play reaches).
- Spoiler-sensitive pages use a `req` key (`item:`, `region:`, `civ:`, `species:`) and spoiler-sensitive
  advancements are `hidden`; their meaning is documented only in `docs/private/`.
